subject: VALUE clause
notes: RE-RECORDED 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB598) — the SUBJECT of each sentence, which this row had right for what SR4 forbids and wrong for what it admits. SR4 is three sentences: a category sentence, then 'Alphanumeric literals in the VALUE clause of an elementary item shall not exceed the size indicated by an explicit PICTURE clause' and 'Alphanumeric literals in the VALUE clause of an alphanumeric group item shall not exceed the size of the group item'. The 2026-09-04 landing (PB206) closed both size sentences, which had silently TRUNCATED, and this row was recorded CONFORMS on that evidence — but the screen it landed was reached by the three level-88 call sites in BindCondition carrying the CONDITIONAL VARIABLE's size, so it also applied the elementary-item sentence to a subject neither sentence names. `01 XV PIC X. 88 XC VALUE "cd".` became COBOL1740, legal source rejected, and GnuCOBOL differential case syn_misc:388 flipped from AGREE_ACCEPT to WE_REJECT_THEY_ACCEPT. A Format-3 entry is `88 condition-name-1 value-clause .` (13.16.2), which admits no PICTURE clause, so no EXPLICIT picture indicates a size; SR33 makes that level-88 entry the subject of the entry; 8.5.1.3.2 item 3 gives a condition-name entry 'no true concept of level', so it is neither of 8.5.1.3.1's record subdivisions; and 13.18.63.4 GR19 gives it its conditional variable's characteristics only IMPLICITLY, which is exactly what 'explicit' excludes. The three subjects the rule addresses are now a TYPE, ValueSubject, built only by ForElementary / ForGroup / ForConditionName, so a call site cannot compose a size the standard does not give it. The category sentence is unaffected and still binds a condition-name (SR4 is an ALL FORMATS rule). And the standard defines what an oversize condition-name literal MEANS, which a size rule would make dead text: 8.8.4.5.3 item 2 sends the comparison to the relation-condition rules, so it never compares equal; 14.9.39.4 GR6 -> 13.18.63.4 GR7 -> 14.6.8.5 places it 'with space fill or truncation to the right'. The 85 golden pb598_condition_name_value_size derives every one of those answers from the rules before measuring them; the pb206 negatives and ConditionNameValueSizeTests.TheSizeSentencesStillBindAnElementaryAndAGroupSubject are the drift proof that withholding the size from a condition-name did not withhold it from the two subjects the sentences do name (that test was measured RED against a deliberately over-withholding build). A FIGURATIVE operand remains exempt by rule (8.3.3.6.4 GR2). Error at every edition: Annex E.2 item 27's 2023 size change is scoped to numeric-edited items (COBOL1570).
